subtitle: What running the checks teaches us about the checks.

findings.title: Cold Read PASS is asymptotic on a rich card.
findings.detail: A fresh cold reader (the Cold Read gives a blind model ONLY the card and asks whether it can act) surfaces new clarifications every iteration no matter how much is inlined — running it on the Sitz drawer, 9 successive iterations each fixed the flagged gaps and each drew ~4 new ones. The gaps travelled from BROKEN (hardcoded pills, false 'sitz_layers EMPTY', no runnable commands, a non-re-runnable per-move coder) to POLISH (wording, a naming convention) — but the verdict stayed PARTIAL throughout. The honest signal is the TRAJECTORY (broken→polish), not a binary stamp. Implication: PASS should mean 'no BROKEN gaps + all remaining limits honestly flagged', not 'zero clarifications a fresh reader could want' — otherwise no rich card ever passes and the bar measures verbosity, not self-sufficiency.

validity.question: Does a check passing mean the engine is good — or that the card is exhaustive?
validity.answer: They come apart. A card can be genuinely self-sufficient (every command, definition, and DB pointer present) and still draw fresh Cold Read nits, because a blind reader's appetite for clarification is unbounded. Grade the check on whether BROKEN gaps remain, and read the iteration trajectory as the real quality signal.
